title: Machined surfaces are a geometric heuristic (8 largest planar areas + every hole), not the drawing
area: Machining feature recognition / machined v unmachined surfaces
existing: Kernel face rows = the 8 largest distinct planar-face areas ≥ 400 mm² of ANY orientation (cad-geometry-engine.py:354, 441-446); defaultInclude near_net costs every face row and every hole (feature-machining.ts:120-123). Drafted walls are included. No drawing roughness / datum / tolerance input; ticks only on the screen forms.
evidence: P2 + P4-C1 (MODELLED yoke): 22 planar faces machined incl. 8 faces carrying 5° draft and 8 I-beam flange faces; design intent (FORGE_modelled_parts.py) = 4 eye faces + 2 bores.
impact: Yoke £16.83 → £10.18 (−39.5 %) when only the eye faces are machined (machining-centre min 9.18 → 3.17; as-forged 2.316 → 1.818 kg). On the genuine parts the error cannot be measured without their drawings.
correctMethod: Machined surfaces come from the finished drawing (surface-texture symbols with "material removal required", toleranced / datum features) or from the difference between the raw and the finished geometry; a face with process draft along the pull is as-made.
source: ISO 1302:2002 / ISO 21920-1:2021 (surface texture indication, machining required); ISO 8062-3:2007 (machined features carry RMA); the tool's own draftAnalysis
inputsNeeded: drawing roughness symbols mapped to CAD faces (the reader already extracts finish.roughness and gdt.datum); or an as-cast/as-forged CAD; engineer confirmation per face in the viewer
proposedLogic: face.machined = linkedRoughnessSymbol(machiningRequired) OR toleranceTighterThan(DCTG/EN10243 grade) OR inFinishedNotInRaw; exclude faces with draft ≥ process minimum; make the set an answer (one decision, faces listed) used by headless and screen alike; remove the top-8 cap.
acceptance: Yoke: machined set = 4 eye faces + 2 bores. On ≥ 3 genuine drawing/CAD pairs: machined-face recall and precision ≥ 95 % against the drawing's symbols, checked by an engineer.

title: Machining allowance is one uniform per-process constant; no RMA/DCTG, no size, no per-feature, no roughing/finishing split
existing: Castings: sand ferrous 3.0 / sand 2.0 / gravity 1.5 / investment 1.0 / HPDC 0.5 mm a side on every machined face and cored bore (machining-time.ts:379-390). Closed-die forgings: IS 3469 Table 1.5 by greatest dimension (forging.ts:276-292); turning stock 2 mm unsourced (machining-time.ts:696); other forging routes unsourced. Drawing never read for it.
evidence: Bracket hand re-calc 54.5 cm³ = 18,166 mm² × 3 mm; P4-A/B sensitivity. | A v B (a-v-b.json): B uses ISO 8062 RMA + CT/4 by largest dimension: 1.55 mm (bracket, 133 mm), 2.35 mm (Part1, 270 mm), 3.6 mm (PRCR002), 3.0 mm (knuckle); A 1.5 mm for any gravity casting, 3.0 mm for any sand iron. Part1 metal A £4.13 v B £4.39.
impact: Per ±1.5 mm of stock: bracket ±£0.31 (±2.9 %), PRCR002 ±£0.88 (±3.2 %); knuckle forging −£0.38/+£0.59 (−2.0/+3.0 %) for 1.5/4 mm. Machining time does not move at all (bracket HMC 4.73 min at 1.5–6 mm), so the cutting cost of extra stock is never charged.
correctMethod: Castings: raw dimension from the finished dimension, the required machining allowance (RMA) for the RMA grade and the casting's largest dimension, and the casting tolerance (DCTG): ISO 8062-3 gives R = F + 2·RMA + CT/2 for an external feature machined both sides (other cases per the standard). Forgings: EN 10243-1 tolerances plus a machining allowance (IS 3469 Part I Table 1.5 or the customer's standard). Roughing and finishing stock split per feature from the tolerance/Ra.
source: ISO 8062-3:2007 (RMA grades, DCTG); EN 10243-1:1999 (closed-die steel forging tolerances); IS 3469 (Part I):1974 Table 1.5 — exact table values to be read from the standards (not reproduced here)
inputsNeeded: RMA grade and DCTG from the drawing general note or the foundry; EN 10243-1 grade (F/E) for forgings; per-feature allowance symbols where drawn; raw CAD when available
proposedLogic: stock(face) = RMA(grade, largest dim) + CT(DCTG, nominal)/2 (one side) per face; same per bore (diametral); cutting time = roughing passes for stock beyond the finishing ap + finishing pass; flag stock < minimum chip for the tool or > 2× RMA as an inconsistency.
acceptance: As-cast/as-forged weight within ±3 % of the foundry/forge weight or raw-CAD volume on ≥ 3 genuine pairs; machining minutes increase monotonically with stock; insufficient-stock flag fires on a constructed case.

title: No raw-to-finished model: one finished CAD + one drawing; no drawing pair, no raw CAD, drawing dimensions / GD&T / Ra extracted but never costed
existing: cad.ts:773-776 accepts one CAD and one drawing; engineering-data packs bind only family, grade, tolerance class, safety, pressure-tight, finish, impregnation, temper; dimension / gdt / roughness / hole / thread parameters go to notCosted; part number / revision read but not reconciled with the CAD.
evidence: Code read (dictionary.ts:23-105, commodity/*.ts, reconcile.ts:394-416, title-block.ts:18-46).
impact: Not quantifiable without genuine raw + finished pairs; it is the root cause of CF-01, CF-02 and CF-06.
correctMethod: A component record holding Stage A (as-cast/as-forged drawing + optional raw CAD) and Stage B (machined drawing + finished CAD), associated by part number / revision / units, with a feature map raw → finished (created, enlarged, finished, untouched).
source: Brief Phase 2; ISO 8062-3 / EN 10243-1 for the raw tolerances
inputsNeeded: second drawing upload with a stage tag; optional raw STEP; title-block identity of both
proposedLogic: Read both drawings with the existing reader; reconcile identity (number, revision, units) and refuse a mismatch; match features by position/axis to the finished CAD (the reader already proposes CAD hole candidates); compute per-feature stock = raw − finished dimension; feed CF-01/CF-02.
acceptance: On ≥ 2 genuine pairs: pair association correct, identity mismatch refused, per-feature stock table produced and signed off by an engineer; costing unchanged when only one drawing is supplied (CAD-only baseline preserved).

title: Forging material balance: billet = as-forged ÷ 0.675 (unsourced) with flash fixed at 10 %; 25.7 % of every billet is un-itemised "scale, crop, wad"
existing: forging.ts:489-500 + FLASH_FRACTION closed-die 0.10 (:75-81) + forging-advisor.ts yieldBand [0.55, 0.80] (labelled not sourced). flashGeometry() (forging.ts:452-459) computes a flash land for the trim press but not the flash mass. Scale not modelled; whole loss credited at steel scrap £0.20/kg.
evidence: P7: knuckle billet 5.697 kg, un-itemised 1.464 kg; hub 1.212 kg; yoke 0.881 kg — all exactly 25.7 % of billet. | A v B (a-v-b.json): Hub flange: A billet 4.72 kg (as-forged 3.185 ÷ 0.675) v B 3.95 kg (raw 3.425 + flash 0.348 + wad 0.145 + scale 0.75 % + excess 3 %); metal net of credits +£0.91 pre-OH. A forging is lighter than B but its billet ratio (1.48 v 1.15) drives the gap.
correctMethod: Billet = as-forged + flash (flash-line perimeter × land width × flash thickness × density, the geometry the trim-press rule already computes) + pierced wad (π/4 · d² · web thickness) + scale loss (% of billet by heating method) + end crop / kerf; recoverable = flash + wad + crop; non-recoverable = scale.
source: needs a source for scale % by heating method and flash land ratios (ASM Handbook Vol. 14A Metalworking: Bulk Forming is the usual reference — values to be read, not assumed)
inputsNeeded: flash land proportions, scale % (induction v gas), wad thickness (from the kernel bore + web), forge shop yield data where available
proposedLogic: compute each loss term explicitly; yieldFraction becomes an output, checked against the band as a plausibility range; credit scale at 0.
acceptance: Material balance prints every term and closes to 0.001 kg; on ≥ 1 genuine forging, billet within ±5 % of the forger's cut weight.

title: Setup / clamping count: kernel caps directions at +X/+Y/+Z from ALL faces; HMC cell assumes ≤ 4 directions in one clamping; 5-axis one setup
existing: _compute_setup_count (cad-geometry-engine.py:1933-2006) clusters every B-rep face normal, merges +N/−N (|dot|) and keeps labels +X/+Y/+Z only (max 3); routing-optimiser.ts:301-307 volume cell 1 clamping when dirs ≤ 4; :295 5-axis 1 setup for near-net.
evidence: P3: machined features need 7 (bracket), 8 (PRCR002), 9 (knuckle), 11 (Part1) approach directions; no single rotary axis reaches them (greedy ≥ 2 clampings each). All costed with 1.
impact: P4-D (2 clampings): bracket +£0.39 (+3.6 %), PRCR002 +£0.68 (+2.5 %), knuckle +£0.97 (+5.0 %), Part1 (machining) +£1.27 (+3.3 %); fixtures double.
correctMethod: Setups from the approach directions of the MACHINED features (signed), the clamped datum face, and the reach of the chosen kinematics (3-axis: one direction; 4th axis: directions ⊥ the rotary axis; 5-axis trunnion: hemisphere minus the clamped face).
source: machine kinematics (maker specifications); engineering practice — no tabulated source needed for the geometric test
inputsNeeded: machined-face set (CF-01), hole approach side (blind holes), datum faces from the drawing
proposedLogic: minimum set cover of signed directions by clampings for each machine class, plus the datum/clamp face; feed the count to fixtures, handling, setup and programming.
acceptance: Bracket, PRCR002, knuckle, Part1 costed with ≥ 2 HMC clampings; a single-face part stays at 1; unit test with constructed parts per kinematics.

title: Machining time independent of stock and tolerance: one finish pass per face and bore; no semi-finish / fine bore / ream / grind / hone
existing: nearNetMachiningTime (machining-time.ts:397-432) faces one finishing face-mill pass (cutting-catalogue.ts:240-248); cored bores one boring pass at f 0.2 + 0.25 min (feature-machining.ts:397-402); reaming removed; ground bearing seats "extra" (machining-time.ts:520); finishFactor only typed on the form.
evidence: P4-A: HMC minutes unchanged 1.5–6 mm stock; P6 halving the boring feed (≈ a second pass). | A v B (a-v-b.json, minutes at B's basis): on the knuckle HMC A cuts ≈ 2.9 min v B 3.8 min (B roughs + finishes faces and bores the H7 seat); on PRCR002 B rough- and finish-bores the king-pin bores in OP10 + OP30; A one finish pass per face and bore everywhere.
impact: Second bore pass ≈ +£0.26 (PRCR002), +£0.39 (knuckle); grinding/honing of bearing seats not quantified (needs drawing tolerances).
correctMethod: Passes from stock depth and the insert/cutter ap limit; finishing strategy from IT grade / Ra (e.g., H7 bore → semi-finish + finish bore or ream; Ra ≤ 0.8 µm → grind/hone).
source: cutting data already sourced (cutting-catalogue.ts); tolerance → process capability tables need a source (e.g., ISO 286 IT grades v process capability charts in a machining handbook)
inputsNeeded: stock per feature (CF-02); tolerance and Ra per feature from the drawing
proposedLogic: n_rough = ceil((stock − finishStock) / ap_max); add finish op by capability table; time each pass with the existing catalogue rows.
acceptance: Machining minutes rise with stock; an H7 bearing bore gets a finish op; regression on the reference part (tests/reference-part.test.ts) still reconciles.

title: Near-net "spindle" lathe operation fires on parts with no spindle (knuckle 9 %, yoke 9.1 % ≥ 8 % threshold)
existing: nearNetTurnedAreaCm2 (machining-time.ts:525-528): external revolved area ≥ 20 cm² and ≥ 8 % of the surface → CNC lathe op + dedicated lathe fixture + load op + turning stock in the raw weight (MIN_NEAR_NET_TURNED_SHARE :490 set between the stub axle 16.5 % and the knuckle 9 % — the knuckle is above it).
evidence: Knuckle forging op "Turning — spindle on the CNC lathe (journals, taper, shoulders)"; yoke the same on its Ø50 eye ODs.
correctMethod: Turning only for revolved features the drawing requires machined (toleranced/Ra) and that a lathe can hold; otherwise interpolate on the machining centre or leave as-made.
source: drawing (CF-01/CF-03)
inputsNeeded: machined-feature set; a lathe-holdability check (part envelope v swing, balance)
proposedLogic: turn a revolved feature only when it is in the machined set; choose lathe v circular interpolation by cost.
acceptance: Knuckle and yoke: no lathe op unless the drawing machines the revolved surface; stub axle keeps its spindle op.

title: No operation sequence or datum scheme; per-side ops apportioned by ALL-face counts; datum-related features split across machines
existing: buildOperationPlan (machining.ts:384-533): one op per kernel direction with millMin × (faces in direction ÷ all faces); drilling and boring as single ops; no OP numbers, no datums, no tools per op.
evidence: Bracket +Z/+X/+Y = 1.476/0.954/0.708 min from 108/70/52 of 230 faces; hub flange Ø60 bore bored on the 5-axis mill apart from the lathe op 10/op 20 turning the OD; lathe op 10/op 20 charged ONE load.
impact: Hub flange: missing second lathe load ≈ £0.46 before overhead/margin (≈ +£0.55, +4 %); the per-side split misattributes cost but does not change the total.
correctMethod: OP10/OP20… built from datum features (drawing datums A/B/C), feature accessibility and tolerance relationships (features related by tight position/runout in the same clamping).
source: drawing GD&T (ISO 1101 / ISO 5459 datums)
inputsNeeded: datums and tolerance frames (already extracted: gdt.frame, gdt.datum)
proposedLogic: group machined features by clamping (CF-05) honouring "same-setup" constraints from GD&T; sequence datum-establishing features first; one handling per chucking.
acceptance: Hub flange bore and OD in one lathe set-up; every op lists its features, tools, machine and setup; times per op sum to today's total where the content is unchanged.

title: Machining scrap not costed on cast + machine, casting or forging secondary machining
existing: cast-and-machine.ts (rules) :97-103 DROPS machining.rejectRate ("the casting module's reject rate covers the part"); forging/casting modules append secondary ops without a reject uplift.
evidence: Code read; MACHINING_REJECT 2 % applies only to machining-from-solid. | A v B (a-v-b.json): B charges 1 % machining scrap (£0.06–0.12) + scrap-loaded secondary on rejected castings; A none.
impact: Estimated +2.0 %: bracket +£0.21, PRCR002 +£0.54 (2 % of factory base, overhead + margin on it — P6, an estimate, not a re-cost).
correctMethod: Scrap at machining scraps the casting/forging plus the machining already done; foundry-attributable rejects found at machining are a separate rate (often charged back to the foundry).
source: needs a source for typical machining scrap rates (plant data)
inputsNeeded: machining scrap %, share attributable to casting defects
proposedLogic: uplift primary + machining cost by 1/(1 − machiningScrap); credit the scrapped part at scrap price.
acceptance: A 2 % machining scrap raises the cast + machine cost by the computed amount and is shown in the material balance.

title: Casting yield (gating / risers) is a band midpoint, not a feeding design
existing: casting.yieldFraction rule (casting.ts:800-818): band midpoints (sand steel 0.525, ductile 0.625, gravity Al 0.6).
evidence: Provenance cam-cast-yield on every cast run.

source: foundry method design references (e.g., modulus method in standard foundry texts) — needs a source to be chosen
inputsNeeded: section modulus (kernel can supply V/S per region), alloy shrinkage
proposedLogic: feeder count/size from hot-spot moduli; gating ratio by process; yield = casting ÷ poured as output, banded as a check.

title: Core cost is a band by undercut-face count, unrelated to the cored-bore rule

impact: Not quantifiable without a core-shop quote (confirms the CLAUDE.md statement that core cost is not built up).

title: Non-cutting time is a fixed approach allowance per feature (0.06–0.5 min, unsourced) — 28–76 % of machining minutes
existing: feature-machining.ts:145 ALLOWANCE_MIN {drill 0.15, microDrill 0.06, borePass 0.25, face 0.20, blind 0.10, tap 0.10, feature 0.30, helical 0.50, land 0.20} added to every feature instance; tool changes 2.2 s on top; no per-operation model of rapids, indexing, probing.

title: Forge-line die setting and per-operation set-ups are not costed; pre-heat-treat grinding, polishing and marking are absent

impact: Per-piece set-up 13-63x lower in the tool than in the 1972 record (era and lot size included).
correctMethod: Set-up per operation and per die change, amortised over the lot; a grinding operation where the drawing calls a ground surface.
source: supplier set-up data needs a source
inputsNeeded: lot sizes, die life between re-sinks, ground-surface callouts
